source: Curated, weighted phrase corpus for Sentinel. Built from public scam guidance and phishing/smishing research datasets. Weights are evidence-strength signals, not calibrated probabilities.

returns.title: Known scam wording about returns
returns.description: The message uses phrases commonly used to promise returns that real investments cannot guarantee.

payment.title: Payment method used in scams
payment.description: The message asks for a payment method that is difficult to trace or reverse.

secrecy.title: Known scam wording about secrecy
secrecy.description: The message asks you to keep the deal from people who could help you check it.

urgency.title: Known scam wording about urgency
urgency.description: The message uses pressure or scarcity language to stop you from checking the offer.

withdrawal.title: Known scam wording about withdrawals
withdrawal.description: The message links withdrawals to fees, targets, or further payments. That is a common way to keep victims paying.

contact.title: Known scam opening lines
contact.description: The message uses an opening line commonly used by investment or romance scammers.

insider.title: Known scam wording about inside information
insider.description: The message claims access to non-public information or an announcement before the market knows.

prediction.title: Known scam wording about price moves
prediction.description: The message predicts a large, fast price move, a pattern common in pump-and-dump schemes.

group.title: Known scam wording about private groups
group.description: The message invites you into a private group where scammers can control what you see.

credentials.title: Known phishing wording
credentials.description: The message asks you to send or enter a password, one-time code, or wallet recovery phrase.

account.title: Known account-notice wording
account.description: The message uses account-notice wording that scammers often copy. Open the official app or type the address yourself.

investment.title: Known investment-pitch wording
investment.description: The message uses wording common in unsolicited investment pitches. Verify the firm and the offering independently.

minimum.title: Known minimum-investment wording
minimum.description: The message asks for a large minimum commitment before you can verify the offer.

recovery.title: Known recovery-scam wording
recovery.description: The message offers to recover lost money for an upfront fee, a common follow-up scam.

impersonation.title: Known impersonation wording
impersonation.description: The message uses wording that imitates a bank, company, or authority.

threat.title: Known threat-based scam wording
threat.description: The message uses threats of arrest, legal action, or a frozen account to force a payment.

regulation.title: Known unregulated-seller wording
regulation.description: The message suggests the seller is not registered or regulated. Check them with a financial regulator.

offshore.title: Known offshore or tax-free pitch
offshore.description: The message uses offshore or tax-free language that makes the seller harder to verify.

too_good.title: Known too-good-to-be-true wording
too_good.description: The message promises easy money, prizes, or instant profits.

testimonial.title: Known fake-proof wording
testimonial.description: The message uses profit screenshots or group testimonials, which scammers can fake.

romance.title: Known romance-scam wording
romance.description: The message uses affectionate language common in relationship investment scams.

taxes.title: Known tax-fee scam wording
taxes.description: The message asks for an upfront tax or fee before money can be released.

prizes.title: Known prize or giveaway wording
prizes.description: The message says you won or can claim a prize. Scammers use this to collect fees or account details.

delivery.title: Delivery or parcel scam wording
delivery.description: The message claims a parcel, package, or delivery needs attention, often to collect a fee or link click.

account_threat.title: Account suspension or verification pressure
account_threat.description: The message claims an account is locked, limited, or at risk and pushes you to verify it through the message.

tech_support.title: Tech support scam wording
tech_support.description: The message claims a device is infected or hacked and pushes you toward a support call or remote-access tool.

job_offer.title: Job or task scam wording
job_offer.description: The message offers easy work, task-based pay, or reshipping, a common way to recruit money mules.

loan.title: Loan or debt-relief scam wording
loan.description: The message promises a guaranteed loan or debt relief and may ask for an upfront fee.

tax_refund.title: Tax refund or IRS impersonation wording
tax_refund.description: The message claims a refund, rebate, or tax problem needs immediate verification or payment.

utility.title: Utility disconnection pressure
utility.description: The message threatens to disconnect a utility service unless you pay or verify immediately.

subscription.title: Subscription renewal or billing wording
subscription.description: The message claims a subscription renewed, expired, or has a billing problem. Verify it in the official app.

crypto.title: Crypto or wallet scam wording
crypto.description: The message pushes wallet validation, seed phrases, airdrops, crypto ATMs, or moving money to a safer account.

gambling.title: Casino or betting spam
gambling.description: The message promotes a casino, betting bonus, free spins, or gambling credit. Gambling spam is a top bulk-SMS category and frequently hides malware or subscription traps.

alcohol_delivery.title: Missed-delivery or alcohol-order spam
alcohol_delivery.description: The message claims a delivery was missed or an alcohol order is pending and pushes you to reschedule through a link.

missed_call.title: Missed-call / call-back spam
missed_call.description: The message reports a missed call or voicemail from an unknown number. Wangiri-style call-back scams rely on these notices.

support.title: Technical/support impersonation
support.description: Impersonation of tech support (Best Buy/Geek Squad, Microsoft, Apple) pressuring to call.
